title: Custom domains
standfirst: Putting an agent behind your own hostname is a feature some providers sell, some leave to a proxy you run, and several do not offer at all.
idea: A custom domain is an HTTPS hostname you control, pointed at a port inside the sandbox. It matters when the URL is the product: a client-facing demo, a webhook receiver, or an agent whose address should not be a provider subdomain that changes.

There are three levels. Native: the provider issues a certificate for your hostname and routes it. Do-it-yourself: the provider gives you a stable hostname and you put your own proxy in front. Absent: no documented path, and the preview URL is what you have.
The differences are in the details: whether you can delegate a subdomain or must move a whole domain's nameservers, whether certificates are automatic, and whether the domain survives a resume.

splits.heading: Native, self-serve domains
body: Runtime routes a sandbox's web port at your hostname with HTTPS. boxd lets you point one domain at a machine or delegate a wildcard subdomain to the whole organisation, and issues certificates automatically. Blaxel's preview URLs support optional auth and custom domains.

quote.text: boxd verifies your DNS and issues TLS certificates automatically.

splits.heading: Do it yourself, or not at all
body: Sandboxer calls first-class custom domains a roadmap item and documents a CNAME plus your own TLS termination. E2B's guide sets up a customer-operated GCP VM running Caddy and Cloudflare DNS to proxy requests to the sandbox. Boat explicitly does not support custom domains.

quote.text: We will set up a GCP VM running Caddy server with Docker and Cloudflare DNS to proxy the requests to the Sandboxes.

splits.heading: Not published is not the same as no
body: InstaBox, Morph, Sprites and Vercel Sandbox publish no sandbox custom-domain feature. InstaBox's API has no customDomain or cname field and its URL is a fixed vendor subdomain; a community report says Sprites lack custom domains the way regular Fly VMs have them; Vercel's domains apply to deployments, not Sandbox ports. For these, the honest answer is that no native path is published.

watchFor: Whether you must move a whole domain's nameservers or can delegate one subdomain.
Whether the certificate is issued automatically.
Whether the domain survives a stop and resume, or must be re-pointed.
Whether the feature is native or a proxy you operate.
Whether the domain is for sandboxes or only for deployed apps.

rows.scenario: Possible only by delegating a whole dedicated domain's nameservers; a subdomain of your existing domain cannot be registered.
rows.note: Custom domains are supported, but only by delegating a whole dedicated domain's nameservers; a subdomain of an existing domain cannot be registered.

source.quote: Custom domain | `https://{label}.yourdomain.com` mirrors all of the above

rows.scenario: Preview URLs support custom domains, with optional auth.
rows.note: Preview URLs back a running sandbox with optional auth and custom domains.

source.quote: Render an application in real-time through a direct preview URL backed by a running Blaxel sandbox, with optional auth and custom domains.

rows.scenario: Explicitly unsupported: a CNAME to on.boat.dev does not work, and certificates are issued only for on.boat.dev names.
rows.note: Custom domains are explicitly unsupported. A CNAME to an on.boat.dev name does not work, and certificates are issued only for on.boat.dev names.

source.quote: boat does not support custom domains.

rows.scenario: Point one domain at the machine or delegate a wildcard subdomain to the organisation; DNS is verified and TLS issued automatically.
rows.note: Point one domain at a machine or delegate a wildcard subdomain to the organisation; boxd verifies DNS and issues TLS certificates automatically.

source.quote: boxd verifies your DNS and issues TLS certificates automatically.

rows.scenario: A wildcard DNS record and a Worker route send demo.acme.com to your Worker, which forwards to the sandbox.
rows.note: Not a sandbox feature: a wildcard DNS record and a Worker route send every preview hostname to your Worker. TLS and authentication are yours.

source.quote: A wildcard DNS record and the route `*.example-previews.com/*` send every preview hostname to your Worker.

rows.scenario: Not native: you host a preview proxy under demo.acme.com, and it starts stopped sandboxes before forwarding.
rows.note: No native custom domain. The documented route is your own preview proxy, which can also start stopped sandboxes before forwarding.

source.quote: host your proxy under your own domain

rows.scenario: No native feature: the documented path is a customer-operated GCP VM running Caddy and Cloudflare DNS in front of the sandbox.
rows.note: No native custom domain. The documented path is a customer-operated GCP VM running Caddy and Cloudflare DNS in front of the sandbox.

source.quote: We will set up a GCP VM running Caddy server with Docker and Cloudflare DNS to proxy the requests to the Sandboxes.

rows.scenario: No custom-domain support is published, and the public-port URL is a fixed vendor subdomain.
rows.note: No custom-domain support is published. The public-port URL is a fixed vendor subdomain, and the OpenAPI PublicPort object has only port, name, url and machineId, with no customDomain or cname field. No roadmap entry exists.

source.quote: The URL is `https://<port>-<machine id without m_>.<domain>/`.

rows.scenario: Documented for deployed app services, not for sandbox preview URLs; a preview stays on the provider hostname.
rows.note: Custom domains are documented for deployed app services, not for sandbox preview URLs. A sandbox preview stays on the provider's hostname.

rows.scenario: Available on Team and Enterprise only: add NS records to Modal's nameservers and ask on Slack to finish onboarding.
rows.note: Custom domains for sandbox tunnels are on Team and Enterprise, with a manual setup step: NS records plus a Slack request.

source.quote: Custom domains for Sandbox tunnels are available on the Team and Enterprise plans.

rows.scenario: No custom-domain feature appears in the documentation, API or terms; an HTTP service is served on a provider hostname.
rows.note: No custom-domain feature appears in the documentation, API or terms. An HTTP service can be exposed, but it is served on a provider hostname.

rows.scenario: The web port can run at your hostname with HTTPS, verified by DNS records and a Let's Encrypt certificate.
rows.note: A sandbox's web port can run at your own hostname with HTTPS, verified by DNS records and a certificate from Let's Encrypt.

source.quote: **Custom domain:** a sandbox's web port at your own hostname, with HTTPS.

rows.scenario: A roadmap item: the documented workaround is a CNAME to the hosted hostname with your own TLS termination.
rows.note: First-class custom domains are on the roadmap; the documented workaround is a CNAME to the hosted hostname with your own TLS termination.

source.quote: First-class custom domains are on the roadmap.

rows.scenario: No native support documented; a community report from April 2026 says Sprites lack custom domains the way regular Fly VMs have them.
rows.note: No native custom-domain support is documented. A community report from April 2026 says Sprites lack custom domains and certificates the way regular Fly VMs do; current support was not confirmed, so treat a proxy as the only known path.

source.quote: Sprites don’t have custom domains and certs the way regular Fly VMs do.

rows.scenario: Attaching your own domain to a Sandbox port was not confirmed; Vercel domains apply to deployments, a different product.
rows.note: Attaching a customer's own domain to a Sandbox port was not confirmed. Vercel domains apply to deployments, a different product; ask whether a separately managed proxy is supported.

source.quote: Run untrusted or agent-generated code in isolated Linux microVMs.

scenario.title: Point demo.acme.com at the agent's port
scenario.setup: You own acme.com and want demo.acme.com to reach port 3000 inside the sandbox, with a valid certificate and no proxy for you to run.

beats.what: Either you add a CNAME for one subdomain, or the provider asks you to move the whole domain's nameservers.
The provider issues a certificate, or you terminate TLS yourself in front of the sandbox.
The machine stops overnight. In the morning the hostname either still points at it or has to be re-pointed.

scenario.turn: Only a handful of providers make this a native, self-serve feature with automatic certificates. For the rest the honest answer is a proxy you operate, a whole-domain delegation, or nothing published.

questions: Can I delegate one subdomain with a CNAME, or do I have to move the whole domain's nameservers?
Who issues and renews the certificate, and how long does that take?
Does the hostname survive a stop and resume, or must it be re-pointed?
Is the domain for sandboxes or only for deployed apps?
If it is not native, what exactly do I have to run in front, and who pays for it?
